ns2:section.sectionText: Actual Innocence: Defects in the Criminal Justice System permits undergraduate students to focus on the criminal justice process and its weaknesses. The students review actual cases where convicted defendants who had spent many years in prison were ultimately completely exonerated, and permits analysis of what went wrong at the trial where the individuals were convicted. Identification, false confessions, DNA, jail-house snitches and many more issues which demonstrate flaws in the justice system are explored. The course requires reading, research, classroom presentations and a submitted paper. First Year Discovery Program Course. Students should enroll in only one Discovery course.
